newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 30.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Prosecutors investigating allegations an associate of the president's son received 1 billion won in kickbacks from a business which was bidding for a regional broadcasting project.

- The government and the South Korean Red Cross tentatively decided to accept North Korea's proposal for North and South Red Cross officials to meet in Beijing on May 3 to discuss a speedily delivery of aid to the North.
- Korea's current-account defict amounted to $7.9 billion in the first quarter of 1997, eclipsing about half of the government's deficit-control target of $14 to $16 billion for all of this year.
- The Foreign Ministry told Seoul-based foreign envoys that the South Korean government is not behind the recent frugality campaigns led by civic groups.
- South Korea is planning to introduce daylight-savings starting in April 1998.
